Why this matters for SSC

State questions = guaranteed 2–3 marks. Common asks: capital, formation, CM, Governor, language, famous for. Master the table.

---

India at a glance (as of 2025)

  • Total States: 28
  • Total Union Territories: 8 (after Jammu & Kashmir bifurcation and Ladakh UT)
  • Total number of entities (states + UTs): 36
  • Total districts (as of 2024): ~780+
  • Capital: New Delhi
  • Currency: Indian Rupee (INR)
  • Largest State (by area): Rajasthan (342,239 km²)
  • Smallest State (by area): Goa (3,702 km²)
  • Largest State (by population): Uttar Pradesh (199.8 million, Census 2011)
  • Smallest State (by population): Sikkim (610,577, Census 2011)
  • Largest UT (by area): Ladakh (173,266 km² including Aksai Chin; or 59,146 km² if PoK is included)
  • Smallest UT (by area): Lakshadweep (32 km²)
  • Most populous UT: Delhi (16.8 million, Census 2011)
  • Least populous UT: Lakshadweep (64,473, Census 2011)
  • Oldest language: Tamil (classical status, mother of Dravidian family)
  • State with longest coastline: Gujarat (1,600 km including the disputed Sir Creek area); mainland + island
  • State with longest international border: Bangladesh (with India, 4,096 km; India state: West Bengal has the longest)
  • Highest literacy state: Kerala (94.0%, 2011)
  • Lowest literacy state: Bihar (61.8%, 2011)
  • Highest sex ratio (state): Kerala (1084)
  • Lowest sex ratio (state): Haryana (879)
  • Highest population density (state): Bihar (1106 persons/km²)
  • Lowest population density (state): Arunachal Pradesh (17 persons/km²)
  • Highest per capita income state: Goa (or Delhi if UT)
  • State with most Lok Sabha seats: UP (80)
  • State with most Rajya Sabha seats: UP (31)
  • State with most SC population: UP (~35 million)
  • State with most ST population: Madhya Pradesh (~15 million)
  • State with highest forest cover: Madhya Pradesh (77,482 km²)

Note: Governors and Chief Ministers change frequently. Listed in the format: data may not be the most current (post-2024 elections). For the latest, check Election Commission of India or PIB.

Northern States

#### Jammu & Kashmir (UT, special status)

Note: J&K is a Union Territory since 31 October 2019 (after bifurcation). Earlier (till 2019), J&K was a state with special status under Article 370. So J&K is now a UT, not a state. The state of J&K has been bifurcated into 2 UTs: Jammu & Kashmir (UT, with legislature) and Ladakh (UT, without legislature).

#### Ladakh (UT)

  • Capital: Leh (summer) / Kargil (winter) — officially, Leh is the capital.
  • Largest district: Leh.
  • Mountains: Karakoram, Zanskar, Ladakh range; part of the Trans-Himalayan region.
  • Lakes: Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri, Tso Kar.
  • Languages: Ladakhi, Tibetan, Urdu, Hindi, English.
  • Established: 31 October 2019.

Key concepts

  • 28 states + 8 UTs = 36 entities (post-2019 bifurcation).
  • J&K and Ladakh are UTs (2019), not states.
  • Capital, language, formation, CM, Governor — all need to be memorized.
  • Highest literacy: Kerala; Lowest: Bihar.
  • Highest population: UP; Lowest: Sikkim.
  • Largest by area: Rajasthan; Smallest by area: Goa.

2024–2025 Updates

  • 2024 general election (18th Lok Sabha): BJP-led NDA won with a reduced majority; Congress-led INDIA bloc gained seats. Held April–June 2024.
  • Andhra Pradesh (Jun 2024): TDP–JSP–BJP alliance won. N. Chandrababu Naidu sworn in as CM (4th time), replacing YSRCP's Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy. Pawan Kalyan (JSP) became Deputy CM.
  • Odisha (Jun 2024): BJP won a clear majority for the first time, ending BJD's 24-year rule. Mohan Charan Majhi became CM (with Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo and Prithviraj Harichandan as Deputy CMs).
  • Haryana (Oct 2024): BJP retained power; Nayab Singh Saini continued as CM (replacing Manohar Lal Khattar earlier in 2024).
  • Jharkhand (Nov 2024): JMM-led INDIA bloc won; Hemant Soren returned as CM (4th time).
  • Maharashtra (Nov 2024): Mahayuti (BJP+Shiv Sena+NCP) won; Devendra Fadnavis became CM, with Eknath Shinde (Deputy CM) and Ajit Pawar (Deputy CM).
  • Delhi (NCT) (Feb 2025): BJP won the assembly election after 27 years (ending AAP's two-term rule). New CM sworn in; verify name on the day of exam.
  • J&K Assembly elections were held in phases in Sep–Oct 2024 — the first assembly elections after the 2019 bifurcation. NC–Congress alliance won; Omar Abdullah became CM. J&K remains a UT with legislature.
  • Census 2021 has been delayed; widely expected to be conducted in 2025–2026 (verify).
  • One Nation, One Election — High-level committee (former President Ram Nath Kovind, 2023) submitted a report in 2024 recommending synchronised polls. Bills placed in Parliament in 2024 (verify current status).
  • Telangana (2024) — no assembly election, but A. Revanth Reddy continues as CM (Congress government formed in Nov 2023).
Tip: For SSC, lock in the CMs of the 5 states that elected new governments in 2024 (AP, Odisha, Haryana, Jharkhand, Maharashtra) and the 2025 Delhi CM. Governor data is the most volatile — verify each one with PIB.
